data.declare-the-worlds-component-types#Decla:
Represent each simulated object as an entity and store its per-object values in components. This page uses the particles from Your first simulation.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable): """Where a particle is.""" var x: Float64 """Horizontal coordinate.""" var y: Float64 """Vertical coordinate.""" @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable): """How far a particle moves per unit of time.""" var dx: Float64 """Horizontal speed.""" var dy: Float64 """Vertical speed.""" var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(delta=0.1)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3)) Position and Velocity are components. World[Position, Velocity] declares the component types the world can store. Each HostStorage.add_entity call creates an entity with the given components and returns its handle.
Define components A component is a struct that conforms to component.ComponentType, which requires Copyable and Deinitable. Copyable, Movable satisfies both. An entity holds at most one value of each component type.
A component with no fields is a tag. Its presence carries the information, and filters can require or exclude it like any other component.
Declare the world’s component types World lists every component type at compile time. An entity of World[Position, Velocity] can have either component, both, or neither: in the example, marker has only a Position. Resources live in separate storage and do not appear in this list.
Larecs groups entities with the same set of components into a logical archetype. You need no knowledge of this layout to create entities or run systems over them.
data.keep-entity-handles#Keep entity handles:
An Entity is a copyable ID and generation, not the address of its components. Keep the handle to find the entity again, for example with HostStorage.get.
Removing an entity invalidates its handle. Larecs increments the 32-bit generation before it reuses the ID, so an old handle refers to a new entity only after the same ID has been reused 2³² times. A handle belongs to the world that created it. Do not use it with another world. Structural changes can move an entity’s components in memory. Keep the handle across structural changes, not component references or row indices.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Update entities with systems and kernels for repeated simulation work. Create and remove entities in batches for creating many entities at once. Archetypes, columns, and locations explains how logical composition maps to physical stores and typed component lifecycles.

data:
Choose where a particle kernel runs and how it receives data. Complete Your first simulation and Share time and configuration first. Each guide has its own complete program; the order below follows their dependencies, so later guides build on earlier ones.
Task Result Run threaded host kernels Split one kernel call into chunks that run on host worker threads. Execute on a device Run the same kernel on an accelerator and compare it with the host. Pass local values to kernels Give a kernel a step-local value and get a result back, on the host or a device. Use portable resources Read an owning collection through a kernel view on either target. Reuse unchanged device copies Skip uploads of data that has not changed since the last device call. Coordinate shared writes Compute one shared result from many invocations without a data race.
data.the-portable-particle-model#The portable:
Every program in this section uses the same variant of the particle types:
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 It differs from the first simulation in two ways, both needed for device execution:
The fields are Float32, because Apple GPUs have no 64-bit floating-point arithmetic. The host runs use Float32 too, so host and device compute the same values. Position and Velocity conform to TrivialRegisterPassable. Device execution requires it of every component a kernel accesses, because Larecs copies those components to the device byte by byte. Threaded host execution needs neither change. It accepts any component whose fields hold no pointers and own no memory, such as the Float64 types of the first simulation, with or without the trait. Time needs no trait on any target, because Larecs checks resources by their fields. The guides keep one model so that each program can switch targets without changing its types.
Compatibility and status lists what each target accepts and the limits that apply everywhere. Errors and migration indexes common failures. Work mapping explains how sequential, threaded, and device execution divide rows.

data:
Give the particle kernel a step-local scale and get a particle count back, without storing either value as a world resource. Use a lexical closure when the kernel runs sequentially on the host, and explicit capture slots when the same kernel must also run on a device. Threaded execution accepts neither; pass its inputs through read-only resources or components.
Start with Execute on a device, which introduces the backend parameter. Run threaded host kernels defines thin kernels.
data.borrow-locals-with-a-closure-on-the-host:
Both programs on this page use the portable particle model.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 A lexical closure is a def nested inside another function that names the local variables it uses in a capture list. Here, move is defined inside Move.update and passed to run as a value:
@fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Counts particles through a sequential host closure.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Moves the particles and observes a synchronous captured result. Args: context: Access to the particle world. Raises: Error: If resources, execution, or the visit check fail. """ var scale: Float32 = 2 var visits = 0 def move( rows: KernelContext[ Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity](), Resources().read[Time](), ] ) {imm scale, mut visits}: """Moves each row and counts it through a host borrow. Args: rows: One matching physical store's rows and time. """ ref time = rows.resources.get[Time]() for particle in rows: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale visits += 1 context.run(move) assert_equal(visits, 2) The capture list {imm scale, mut visits} borrows scale read-only and visits mutably. context.run(move) selects the overload that takes a callable value; it runs only sequentially on the host. Larecs calls move once per matching physical store, and visits increases once per row. run returns after the last call, so the assertion sees the final count.
The driver puts the two particles into different physical stores:
def main() raises: """Checks the closure across two matching physical stores. Raises: Error: If setup, execution, or a position check fails. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]() world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity( Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2), Int32(1) ) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Int32](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=1) assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5) assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](climber).y, 1.0) print("PASS: lexical host captures across two stores") The extra Int32 component gives climber a different composition and therefore its own physical store; it does not change which entities move matches. Both particles move once, and visits counts rows across both calls.
From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/lexical_closure.mojo

Args: context: Rows, time, and ordered scale/count capture slots. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() var scale = context.captures.get[0]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale # The count is shared, not one private scalar per device thread. comptime if is_gpu(): if global_idx.x != 0: return context.captures.get[1]() += context.length @fieldwise_init struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System): """Binds local values for one synchronous step.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Checks count copy-back before the system returns. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If binding, execution, or the count check fails. """ var scale: Float32 = 2 var processed: Int32 = 0 context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]( read_capture(scale), mut_capture(processed) ) assert_equal(scale, 2) assert_equal(processed, 37) def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend]() raises: """Checks empty bindings, two physical stores, and a partial device block. Parameters: backend: Target to validate. Raises: Error: If setup, execution, or an assertion fails. Raises: Error: If any executed target fails. """ run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() print("PASS: explicit host captures, including empty matches") comptime if has_accelerator(): run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() print("PASS: actual device captures and synchronous count copy-back") else: print("SKIP: device captures (no accelerator compilation support)") View the source on GitHub
The program above checks explicit slots on the host and, when available, on a device.
data.declare-explicit-slots-for-a-thin-kernel:
A thin kernel cannot borrow locals, but it can declare ordered capture slots with Captures. The system binds a local value to each slot when it calls run, on the host or on a device.
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() comptime locals_spec = Captures[ReadCapture[Float32], MutCapture[Int32]]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources, locals_spec]): """Moves particles and records the processed count with a single writer. Args: context: Rows, time, and ordered scale/count capture slots. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() var scale = context.captures.get[0]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale # The count is shared, not one private scalar per device thread. comptime if is_gpu(): if global_idx.x != 0: return context.captures.get[1]() += context.length Slot 0 is a ReadCapture input; get[0]() returns its value. Slot 1 is a MutCapture output. Every invocation, and on a device every thread, sees the same output value, so only one writer may update it:
On the host, each invocation covers one physical store and adds its own row count, context.length. Sequential invocations never overlap. On a device, one launch covers all rows. comptime if is_gpu() compiles the check only for the device, where only the thread with global index zero adds the packed row count. This works because no thread reads another thread’s result. A thread-zero branch is not a barrier, and it does not make a general reduction safe.
Bind locals in the declared order when the system runs:
@fieldwise_init struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System): """Binds local values for one synchronous step.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Checks count copy-back before the system returns. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If binding, execution, or the count check fails. """ var scale: Float32 = 2 var processed: Int32 = 0 context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]( read_capture(scale), mut_capture(processed) ) assert_equal(scale, 2) assert_equal(processed, 37) read_capture and mut_capture borrow scale and processed until run returns. On the host, the kernel uses the original values. On a device, Larecs uploads every binding on each call and copies the mutable slot back before run returns, so processed holds 37 at the assertion.
From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/captures.mojo A PASS line for the device means the slots were bound, executed, and copied back on the accelerator; a SKIP line means only the host ran.
data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Failure Cause and fix Compile error on the slot count, type, or mutability Bind one value per slot in declaration order, with the declared type. Two slots may share a type; their index distinguishes them. Borrow-checker error on one local One local cannot be bound read-only and mutably in the same call. Use separate values. Compile error for a device capture that owns memory or holds a pointer Device captures copy plain bytes. Use a portable resource for owning data. Wrong result from several writers A mutable slot provides no synchronization. Use one writer, or per-particle output. Compile error for a closure with DEVICE or threaded=True Lexical closures run only sequentially on the host. Use explicit slots for a device. Keep references from capture slots and closure borrows inside the kernel; they must not outlive the call. The capture reference lists the remaining binding rules.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Use portable resources passes owning collections to host and device kernels. Coordinate shared writes covers results from many writers.
data.variations#Variations:
Keep a value between steps A capture lives for one run call. A value that persists between steps, or that owns memory, belongs in a resource or a portable resource.
Produce one result per particle When many invocations or threads contribute to a result, write a per-particle component and reduce it after run, as in Coordinate shared writes.

data:
Skip uploading particle data that has not changed since the last device call. Use this after the kernel already passes the host and device comparison and a measurement shows that uploads matter. Reuse is off by default, set per world, and experimental. Written outputs still copy back to the host after every call.
Start with Execute on a device.
data.check-both-transfer-policies#Check both:
The driver runs the same sequence on the host, on the device with default transfers, and on the device with reuse:
def main() raises: """Checks the same sequence on host, default device, and reused device copies. Raises: Error: If a target or transfer policy changes the result. """ var host = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST](False) print("PASS: host mutation/invalidation sequence") comptime if has_accelerator(): var default = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE](False) var reused = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE](True) assert_equal(reused.x, default.x) assert_equal(reused.y, default.y) assert_equal(reused.x, host.x) assert_equal(reused.y, host.y) print("PASS: actual device default/reused copies and host parity") else: print("SKIP: device-copy reuse (no accelerator compilation support)") Every run ends at (4.5, 7.0).
From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/copy_reuse.mojo A PASS line for the device means both transfer policies ran on the accelerator and matched the host; a SKIP line means only the host sequence ran.
data.complete-program#Complete program: Complete program: examples/particles/copy_reuse.mojo """Checks particle results with default transfers and opt-in copy reuse.""" # SKIP_DEBUG # SKIP_ASAN from std.testing import assert_almost_equal, assert_equal from larecs import ( ExecutionBackend, Filter, KernelContext, Resources, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, World, ) from std.sys import has_accelerator @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System): """Keeps the movement kernel and target independent of copy policy.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Completes movement and eager copy-back. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If preparation or execution fails. """ context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]() def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend](reuse: Bool) raises -> Position: """Runs a mutation sequence under one transfer policy. Parameters: backend: Explicit execution target. Args: reuse: Whether unchanged device copies may skip uploads. Raises: Error: If execution or the expected coordinates disagree. Returns: A snapshot of the walker's final position. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2)) world.reuse_device_copies(reuse) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]()) scheduler.initialize() scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 0.25 _ = scheduler.world.resources.read[Time]().delta _ = scheduler.world.storage.read[Velocity](walker).dx scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 0.5; read calls preserve reuse scheduler.world.resources.get[Time]().delta = 0.5 scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 1.0; get advances the resource revision # This pointer survives a later run; subsequent writes bypass tracking. var time_ptr = Pointer(to=scheduler.world.resources.get[Time]()) scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 1.5 time_ptr[].delta = 1.0 scheduler.world.resources.invalidate_device[Time]() scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 2.5; explicit invalidation refreshes Time scheduler.world.storage.get[Velocity](walker).dx = 2 scheduler.update( steps=1 ) # x = 4.5; component get advances its column revision scheduler.finalize() var result = scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).copy() assert_almost_equal(result.x, 4.5) assert_almost_equal(result.y, 7.0) scheduler.world.reuse_device_copies(False) return result def main() raises: """Checks the same sequence on host, default device, and reused device copies. Raises: Error: If a target or transfer policy changes the result. """ var host = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST](False) print("PASS: host mutation/invalidation sequence") comptime if has_accelerator(): var default = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE](False) var reused = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE](True) assert_equal(reused.x, default.x) assert_equal(reused.y, default.y) assert_equal(reused.x, host.x) assert_equal(reused.y, host.y) print("PASS: actual device default/reused copies and host parity") else: print("SKIP: device-copy reuse (no accelerator compilation support)") View the source on GitHub
data.enable-reuse-for-a-world#Enable reuse fo:
The stage uses the portable particle model and the unchanged movement kernel and system.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System): """Keeps the movement kernel and target independent of copy policy.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Completes movement and eager copy-back. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If preparation or execution fails. """ context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]() The kernel and system do not know about the transfer policy. You enable it on the world with World.reuse_device_copies, as the sequence below does before it moves walker six times:
def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend](reuse: Bool) raises -> Position: """Runs a mutation sequence under one transfer policy. Parameters: backend: Explicit execution target. Args: reuse: Whether unchanged device copies may skip uploads. Raises: Error: If execution or the expected coordinates disagree. Returns: A snapshot of the walker's final position. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2)) world.reuse_device_copies(reuse) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]()) scheduler.initialize() scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 0.25 _ = scheduler.world.resources.read[Time]().delta _ = scheduler.world.storage.read[Velocity](walker).dx scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 0.5; read calls preserve reuse scheduler.world.resources.get[Time]().delta = 0.5 scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 1.0; get advances the resource revision # This pointer survives a later run; subsequent writes bypass tracking. var time_ptr = Pointer(to=scheduler.world.resources.get[Time]()) scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 1.5 time_ptr[].delta = 1.0 scheduler.world.resources.invalidate_device[Time]() scheduler.update(steps=1) # x = 2.5; explicit invalidation refreshes Time scheduler.world.storage.get[Velocity](walker).dx = 2 scheduler.update( steps=1 ) # x = 4.5; component get advances its column revision scheduler.finalize() var result = scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).copy() assert_almost_equal(result.x, 4.5) assert_almost_equal(result.y, 7.0) scheduler.world.reuse_device_copies(False) return result Larecs keeps a revision for each resource and for each component column of a physical store, and advances it whenever the host may have changed that data. With reuse enabled, a device call uploads a resource or column only when the revision of its device copy, the bytes already on the device, differs from the current one. In the sequence:
read calls leave the revisions unchanged, so the second step reuses every input. get through mutable storage advances the revision whether or not you write, so the step after get[Time]().delta = 0.5 uploads Time again. A successful device call leaves the written Position current on both sides, so the next call can skip its upload too. Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.
Retained capacity does not prove that its contents are current.
Larecs keeps device allocations between calls whether or not reuse is enabled; a kept allocation says nothing about whether its bytes are current. With reuse enabled, a read-only portable resource whose source is current skips prepare_device and reuses its view.
data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Symptom Cause and fix The device reads old values A write went through a reference kept from before a run, or a raw pointer. Reacquire references with get after each run, or invalidate the copy. Turn reuse off to confirm the diagnosis. Inputs still upload on most calls Something advances their revisions: a mutable get, a host or threaded kernel that declares a write, a structural change, spatial maintenance, or a filter or selection that packs rows at a different offset. Use read for observation. Written data still downloads Larecs copies written outputs back after every call; reuse skips only uploads. The copy-reuse reference lists every operation that advances a revision.
data.invalidate-a-write-larecs-cannot-see#Inv: Larecs advances a revision when you call get, not when you later write through the reference it returned. The sequence keeps time_ptr across a run and then writes through it, so Larecs cannot see that write. scheduler.world.resources.invalidate_device[Time]() marks the device copy of Time stale, and the next call uploads it again. For writes through raw pointers to several resources or columns, World.invalidate_device_copies marks every device copy stale. Reacquiring a reference with get after each run avoids the problem.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Measure complete simulation steps before you keep this option. Device-copy validity explains how Larecs records which device copies are current.
data.variations#Variations:
Observe values without forcing an upload Use read on storage and resources, or read-only queries, when you only look at values. They keep device copies current.
Turn reuse off world.reuse_device_copies(False) discards the reuse records; the next device call uploads every input again. Calls stay synchronous either way.

data:
Run the particle movement kernel on an accelerator, such as a GPU, and check that it produces the same positions as the host. Use this when a kernel does enough arithmetic per particle to outweigh copying data to the device and back. Device execution is experimental; it needs the repository’s pinned Mojo and MAX environment and a supported accelerator.
Start with Update entities with systems and kernels and Share time and configuration.
data.compare-the-device-with-the-host#Compare:
The driver runs two steps on 37 moving particles and one unmatched marker, once per target, each in a fresh world.
def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend]() raises -> Position: """Runs two steps and checks both coordinates and an unmatched marker. Parameters: backend: Explicit target for this independent simulation. Raises: Error: If setup, execution, or a position check fails. Returns: The sum of the moving particles' final coordinates. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=37) var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3)) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]()) scheduler.run(steps=2) var total = Position(0, 0) for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter](): ref position = particle.get[Position]() assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5) assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0) total.x += position.x total.y += position.y assert_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](marker).x, -3) return total def main() raises: """Reports device execution separately from a hardware skip. Raises: Error: If host checks, device execution, or parity checks fail. """ var host = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() assert_almost_equal(host.x, 18.5) assert_almost_equal(host.y, 37.0) print("PASS: host particle checks") comptime if has_accelerator(): var device = run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() assert_almost_equal(device.x, host.x) assert_almost_equal(device.y, host.y) print("PASS: actual device execution and host/device parity") else: # A skip is an application choice; DEVICE itself never falls back. var empty = World[Position, Velocity]() empty.resources.add(Time(0.25)) var context = SystemContext(empty) with assert_raises(): context.run[move, backend=ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() print("SKIP: device parity (no accelerator compilation support)") Every mover ends at (0.5, 1.0), the marker stays at (-3, -3), and the device sums match the host sums. has_accelerator() decides whether the program attempts the device at all; without support, it checks that a device call raises instead of falling back.
From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/device.mojo A PASS line for the device means the kernel ran on the accelerator and matched the host; a SKIP line means this machine has no supported accelerator and only the host ran.

data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Failure Cause and fix run raises that DEVICE requires accelerator support or a working device context No usable accelerator. Fix the accelerator or toolchain, or select ExecutionBackend.HOST; there is no device fallback. Compile error: every accessed component type must be device-safe Make the component TrivialRegisterPassable, as in the portable model. Only accessed components are checked. Compile error: device resources require pointer-free trivial plain values The resource owns memory or holds a pointer. Use a portable resource for owning data. Compile error: device write-only resources are unsupported Declare an ordinary device resource with read or read_write. Compile error for a lexical closure or threaded=True Device execution needs a thin kernel and cannot be combined with threaded host execution. run raises about a missing resource, even with no matching rows Add every declared resource during setup. A failed device call does not roll back host writes that already happened. The device execution reference covers empty matches, transfer and synchronization failures, and when a world rejects further device work. Transfers and preparation can dominate a small kernel; measure complete simulation steps before choosing a backend.
data.how-device-threads-visit-rows#How device:
On the host, a kernel invocation covers one physical store or one threaded chunk. On a device, one launch covers all packed rows, and each device thread runs the kernel body. The for loop over the context uses grid-stride iteration: each thread starts at its global thread index and advances by the total number of launched threads, so every row is visited exactly once, even when there are more rows than threads.
Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.
One row loop, three invocation mappings.
Code outside the for loop runs once per device thread. A row’s idx is its offset in the packed rows, and row indices are not entity IDs.
data.let-the-filter-decide-what-moves#Let the:
Larecs copies only the data the kernel declares. For each call, it packs the matching rows of every physical store into contiguous device columns, runs the kernel once over all of them, and copies written columns back to their original rows.
Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.
Access declarations determine transfer directions.
Declaration Upload before the kernel Copy back after the kernel include[Position]() Yes Yes read[Velocity](), Resources().read[Time]() Yes No write[T]() No; the kernel must set every row it visits Yes run returns after the kernel finishes and Larecs has copied every written component, read-write resource, and mutable capture back to the host. The next system sees the new values on the host. Rows that the filter does not match stay untouched.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Pass local values to kernels binds a scale and a counter for host and device runs. Use portable resources reads owning collections on the device. Bindings, transfers, and revisions explains packing and copy-back.
data.variations#Variations:
Choose the target at run time The backend is a compile-time parameter. To choose at run time, branch and call each specialization explicitly, for example add Move[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() when has_accelerator() is true and Move[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() otherwise. Larecs itself has no device fallback.
Run on a selection EntitySelection.run accepts the same backend parameter and packs only the selection’s rows.
Pass local values or owning data Use explicit capture slots for a step-local value and portable resources for an owning collection.
Skip unchanged uploads By default, every device call uploads all readable columns and resources. Reuse unchanged device copies skips uploads of data that has not changed since the last call.

data:
Read an owning collection, such as a list of samples, from the particle kernel on both the host and a device. An ordinary resource that owns memory works on the sequential host only, because Larecs cannot copy its heap data to a device byte by byte. A portable resource is a resource source with an adapter. It keeps the owner on the host and gives each kernel a kernel view, a plain value that points to the data on the kernel’s target.
Start with Share values with resources and Execute on a device. Mutable portable resources are experimental; this page uses read-only views.
data.complete-program#Complete program: Complete program: examples/particles/portable_resources.mojo """Moves particles using a buffer and an adapter-backed grid.""" # SKIP_DEBUG # SKIP_ASAN from std.testing import assert_almost_equal, assert_equal from larecs import ( ExecutionBackend, Filter, KernelContext, Resources, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, World, ) from std.sys import has_accelerator from std.testing import assert_raises from larecs import ( BufferResource, DevicePassableResource, ResourceAdapter, ResourceDeviceCache, ) @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 comptime Samples = BufferResource[DType.float32] @fieldwise_init struct Grid(DevicePassableResource): """Owns samples and dimensions on the host.""" comptime Adapter = GridAdapter var values: List[Float32] var width: Int var height: Int @fieldwise_init struct GridView(TrivialRegisterPassable): """Borrows immutable samples in the current target's address space.""" var values: Pointer[Float32, ImmUntrackedOrigin] var width: Int var height: Int def last(self) -> Float32: """Reads the final sample of a validated nonempty grid. Returns: The bottom-right sample. """ return self.values[unsafe_offset=self.width * self.height - 1] struct GridAdapter(ResourceAdapter): """Prepares the same immutable descriptor for either target.""" comptime Source = Grid comptime View[mut: Bool] = GridView @staticmethod def validate(source: Self.Source) raises: """Validates shape and bounds before either target is prepared. Args: source: Current host owner. Raises: Error: If shape arithmetic overflows or sample counts disagree. """ if source.width <= 0 or source.height <= 0: raise Error("Grid dimensions must be positive") if source.width > Int(Int64.MAX) // source.height: raise Error("Grid dimensions overflow") if source.width * source.height != len(source.values): raise Error("Grid shape must match sample count") @staticmethod def bind_host(source: Self.Source) raises -> Self.View[False]: """Borrows the validated owner's samples without copying. Args: source: Owner retained through invocation completion. Returns: Host-local immutable descriptor. """ return { Pointer[Float32, ImmUntrackedOrigin]( unsafe_from_address=Int(source.values.unsafe_ptr()) ), source.width, source.height, } @staticmethod def prepare_device( source: Self.Source, mut cache: ResourceDeviceCache ) raises -> Self.View[False]: """Uploads samples through invocation-owned staging. Args: source: Current validated owner. cache: Source-type and device-context local allocations. Raises: Error: If allocation or upload fails. Returns: Descriptor containing a device-local sample pointer. """ return { cache.upload[Float32](0, Span(source.values)), source.width, source.height, } comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time, Samples, Grid]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Uses source-type lookup to read two portable views. Args: context: Particle rows, plain time, and adapted resources. """ ref samples = context.resources.get[Samples]() ref grid = context.resources.get[Grid]() ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() var scale = samples[0] + grid.last() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale @fieldwise_init struct Move[backend: ExecutionBackend](System): """Runs movement with access-selected resource views.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Binds resources for one complete invocation. Args: context: Access to the particle world. Raises: Error: If validation, preparation, or execution fails. """ context.run[move, backend=Self.backend]() def run_stage[backend: ExecutionBackend]() raises: """Checks owner edits, portable reads, and invalid shape rejection. Parameters: backend: Target to validate independently. Raises: Error: If execution or an assertion fails. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add( Time(0.25), Samples([Float32(1)]), Grid([Float32(0), Float32(0), Float32(0), Float32(2)], 2, 2), ) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2)) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move[backend]()) scheduler.initialize() scheduler.update(steps=1) assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.75) scheduler.world.resources.get[Grid]().values[3] = 3 scheduler.update(steps=1) assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 1.75) assert_almost_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).y, 3.5) assert_equal(scheduler.world.resources.read[Grid]().values[3], 3) scheduler.finalize() # Adapter validation also runs when no entities match. var empty = World[Position, Velocity]() empty.resources.add( Time(0.25), Samples([Float32(1)]), Grid(List[Float32](), 2, 2) ) var context = SystemContext(empty) with assert_raises(): context.run[move, backend=backend]() def main() raises: """Labels executed resource targets separately from hardware skips. Raises: Error: If an executed target fails. """ run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() print("PASS: host buffer/grid views, owner edits, and empty validation") comptime if has_accelerator(): run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() print("PASS: actual device buffer/grid views and particle checks") else: print("SKIP: device resources (no accelerator compilation support)") View the source on GitHub
data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Failure Cause and fix run raises a grid validation error, even with no matching entities The owner is invalid. Make the dimensions match the sample count before the call. Compile error: mutable access requires Adapter.supports_mutation The source is declared writable. Declare it with read, or implement a writer view. Crash or wrong values from a view pointer The view points to memory that does not belong to the owner or the device cache, or an earlier reference changed the owner during the call. Return owner-backed or cache-backed memory only. Stale samples with copy reuse enabled The owner changed through a reference that Larecs does not track. Reacquire it with get after each run, or invalidate it.
data.keep-sources-and-views-valid-during-a-ca:
For the duration of a call, Larecs holds a lease on every bound source: it keeps the source alive and in place, and looking it up, replacing it, or removing it from inside the call raises. Two rules keep views valid:
Keep views, their pointers, and references obtained from them inside the kernel invocation. Do not change, resize, or free the owner through a reference you kept from before the call while the call runs. A lease protects the source’s lifetime; it does not synchronize threads. Structural locks are not mutexes, and neither are leases. The adapter reference lists the remaining rules for adapter authors.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Reuse unchanged device copies avoids repeated uploads. Bindings, transfers, and revisions explains leases, adapter views, and their lifetimes.
data.prepare-the-view-for-each-target#Prepare:
A ResourceAdapter checks the current owner and builds the view for the target of each call.
struct GridAdapter(ResourceAdapter): """Prepares the same immutable descriptor for either target.""" comptime Source = Grid comptime View[mut: Bool] = GridView @staticmethod def validate(source: Self.Source) raises: """Validates shape and bounds before either target is prepared. Args: source: Current host owner. Raises: Error: If shape arithmetic overflows or sample counts disagree. """ if source.width <= 0 or source.height <= 0: raise Error("Grid dimensions must be positive") if source.width > Int(Int64.MAX) // source.height: raise Error("Grid dimensions overflow") if source.width * source.height != len(source.values): raise Error("Grid shape must match sample count") @staticmethod def bind_host(source: Self.Source) raises -> Self.View[False]: """Borrows the validated owner's samples without copying. Args: source: Owner retained through invocation completion. Returns: Host-local immutable descriptor. """ return { Pointer[Float32, ImmUntrackedOrigin]( unsafe_from_address=Int(source.values.unsafe_ptr()) ), source.width, source.height, } @staticmethod def prepare_device( source: Self.Source, mut cache: ResourceDeviceCache ) raises -> Self.View[False]: """Uploads samples through invocation-owned staging. Args: source: Current validated owner. cache: Source-type and device-context local allocations. Raises: Error: If allocation or upload fails. Returns: Descriptor containing a device-local sample pointer. """ return { cache.upload[Float32](0, Span(source.values)), source.width, source.height, } validate runs before every call, including calls that match no entities. It rejects empty or inconsistent grids, so last() never reads out of bounds. bind_host points the view at the owner’s own list; it copies nothing. prepare_device uploads the samples through ResourceDeviceCache slot 0 and returns a view that points to device memory. The cache keeps the device allocation between calls; by default, the samples upload again on every call.
data.request-the-source-type-in-the-kernel#Re:
The kernel declares and looks up resources by their source type:
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time, Samples, Grid]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Uses source-type lookup to read two portable views. Args: context: Particle rows, plain time, and adapted resources. """ ref samples = context.resources.get[Samples]() ref grid = context.resources.get[Grid]() ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() var scale = samples[0] + grid.last() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta * scale position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta * scale Inside move, get[Samples]() returns a ReadBuffer and get[Grid]() returns a GridView, both immutable. Outside a kernel, world.resources.get[Grid]() returns the owning Grid. Larecs registers the adapter when you add the source; there is no separate registration call.
The driver adds both sources, edits the grid between steps, and checks that validation also runs without matching entities:

Raises: Error: If an executed target fails. """ run_stage[ExecutionBackend.HOST]() print("PASS: host buffer/grid views, owner edits, and empty validation") comptime if has_accelerator(): run_stage[ExecutionBackend.DEVICE]() print("PASS: actual device buffer/grid views and particle checks") else: print("SKIP: device resources (no accelerator compilation support)") The first step scales movement by 1 + 2 and ends at x=0.75. From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/portable_resources.mojo A PASS line for the device means the kernel read both views on the accelerator; a SKIP line means only the host ran.
data.variations#Variations:
Write through an adapter GridAdapter supports reading only, so declare its source with read; the Resources[Grid]() default means read-write and fails to compile. An adapter that sets supports_mutation can provide a writable view for sequential host calls, and one that also sets supports_concurrent_mutation can provide it for threaded and device calls. The mutable adapter reference and the scatter example show the hooks and an atomic slot reservation. For most shared output, prefer per-particle results.
Skip unchanged uploads With device-copy reuse enabled, a read-only source that has not changed since the last device call skips prepare_device and reuses its view.

data:
Compute one shared result, the total displacement of all particles, without a data race. Each particle writes its own output in the kernel, and one caller sums the outputs after run returns. This works on every target, including threaded chunks and device threads, where many invocations run at once. For data you own outside the world, Larecs also provides standalone atomic values and guarded values.
Start with Update entities with systems and kernels. Larecs does not bind synchronization primitives to kernels automatically; see compatibility and status.
data.complete-program#Complete program: Complete program: examples/particles/shared_outputs.mojo """Reduces per-particle outputs on one caller and checks standalone primitives.""" from std.testing import assert_almost_equal, assert_equal from larecs import ( ExecutionBackend, Filter, KernelContext, Resources, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, World, ) from std.atomic import Ordering from std.testing import assert_false, assert_true from larecs import AtomicValue, Synchronized @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Displacement(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """A private output for one particle, avoiding a shared kernel counter.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]().write[ Displacement ]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Writes every per-row output before a later single-caller reduction. Args: context: Particle inputs and set-only displacement output. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() var dx = velocity.dx * time.delta var dy = velocity.dy * time.delta position.x += dx position.y += dy particle.set(Displacement(dx, dy)) @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Runs row work before a single-caller reduction.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Reduces completed per-row outputs without a shared kernel write. Args: context: Access to the world after synchronous kernel completion. Raises: Error: If execution or the reduction check fails. """ context.run[move]() var total = Displacement(0, 0) for particle in context.world[].storage.query[ Filter().read[Displacement]() ](): ref value = particle.get[Displacement]() total.x += value.x total.y += value.y assert_almost_equal(total.x, 9.25) assert_almost_equal(total.y, 18.5) def check_primitives() raises: """Checks target-local host primitives independently of ECS bindings. Raises: Error: If an atomic or guard check fails. """ var counter = AtomicValue[UInt32](0) var updates = counter.write_view() assert_equal(updates.fetch_add(1), UInt32(0)) var result = updates.compare_exchange(1, 5) assert_true(result.exchanged) assert_equal(result.observed, UInt32(1)) updates.store[Ordering.RELEASE](7) assert_equal(updates.load[Ordering.ACQUIRE](), UInt32(7)) var state = Synchronized[UInt32](10) var access = state.write_view() var attempt = access.try_read() assert_true(attempt.is_acquired()) var reader = attempt^.take() assert_equal(reader.value(), UInt32(10)) assert_false(access.try_write().is_acquired()) reader^.release() var write_attempt = access.try_write() assert_true(write_attempt.is_acquired()) var writer = write_attempt^.take() writer.value() += 5 writer^.release() var read_attempt = access.try_read() assert_true(read_attempt.is_acquired()) var after = read_attempt^.take() assert_equal(after.value(), UInt32(15)) def main() raises: """Checks particle reduction and standalone host primitives. Raises: Error: If setup, execution, or a check fails. """ var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Displacement]() scheduler.world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = scheduler.world.storage.add_entities( Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), Displacement(0, 0), count=37 ) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=1) check_primitives() print( "PASS: per-particle outputs, single-caller reduction, and host" " primitives" ) View the source on GitHub
data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Failure Cause and fix Wrong totals from a shared resource or capture Several invocations wrote one value. Write per-particle output and reduce after run. try_read or try_write returns Busy The attempt met a conflicting guard, a concurrently changed state, or the reader limit. Do not spin; defer the work to a later pass. Compile error for an ordering, compare-exchange, or guard on an Apple GPU Apple devices support only relaxed or acquire loads, relaxed or release stores, and relaxed add and subtract. Use per-particle output instead. Compile error when an AtomicView or SyncView is in a resource or capture Views do not transfer to kernels. Use per-particle output, or a mutable adapter that manages its own atomic buffer. Ordinary data written next to a relaxed counter is not visible Relaxed operations order nothing else. Use release stores and acquire loads to publish data. Structural locks are not mutexes; neither are resource leases. The synchronization reference lists supported orderings per backend, guard rules, and device memory requirements.

data.reduce-after-the-kernel-returns#Reduce a:
The system sums the outputs once run has returned:
@fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Runs row work before a single-caller reduction.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Reduces completed per-row outputs without a shared kernel write. Args: context: Access to the world after synchronous kernel completion. Raises: Error: If execution or the reduction check fails. """ context.run[move]() var total = Displacement(0, 0) for particle in context.world[].storage.query[ Filter().read[Displacement]() ](): ref value = particle.get[Displacement]() total.x += value.x total.y += value.y assert_almost_equal(total.x, 9.25) assert_almost_equal(total.y, 18.5) run is synchronous, so the query sees every written Displacement. One caller sums all 37 outputs to (9.25, 18.5); nothing writes total concurrently.
The driver creates the particles and also runs the atomic and guard checks shown later on this page:
def main() raises: """Checks particle reduction and standalone host primitives. Raises: Error: If setup, execution, or a check fails. """ var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Displacement]() scheduler.world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = scheduler.world.storage.add_entities( Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), Displacement(0, 0), count=37 ) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=1) check_primitives() print( "PASS: per-particle outputs, single-caller reduction, and host" " primitives" ) From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/shared_outputs.mojo The PASS line means the host reduction and the host primitive checks succeeded.
data.variations#Variations:
Reduce in several passes For a parallel reduction, write partial results to disjoint per-particle or per-group components, then combine them in a later run or on the host. Each pass reads only output that an earlier, finished call wrote.
Use a single writer One designated writer may update a shared value when it does not need other threads’ unfinished results, as the capture count does with global thread zero. A thread-zero branch is not a barrier.
Update data you own with atomic or guarded values These primitives work on storage you own, outside the world:
def check_primitives() raises: """Checks target-local host primitives independently of ECS bindings. Raises: Error: If an atomic or guard check fails. """ var counter = AtomicValue[UInt32](0) var updates = counter.write_view() assert_equal(updates.fetch_add(1), UInt32(0)) var result = updates.compare_exchange(1, 5) assert_true(result.exchanged) assert_equal(result.observed, UInt32(1)) updates.store[Ordering.RELEASE](7) assert_equal(updates.load[Ordering.ACQUIRE](), UInt32(7)) var state = Synchronized[UInt32](10) var access = state.write_view() var attempt = access.try_read() assert_true(attempt.is_acquired()) var reader = attempt^.take() assert_equal(reader.value(), UInt32(10)) assert_false(access.try_write().is_acquired()) reader^.release() var write_attempt = access.try_write() assert_true(write_attempt.is_acquired()) var writer = write_attempt^.take() writer.value() += 5 writer^.release() var read_attempt = access.try_read() assert_true(read_attempt.is_acquired()) var after = read_attempt^.take() assert_equal(after.value(), UInt32(15)) AtomicValue owns a UInt32 or Int32 scalar, and AtomicView borrows it. fetch_add returns the previous value. compare_exchange reports whether it exchanged and which value it observed. Operations use relaxed ordering unless you pass an ordering, such as store[Ordering.RELEASE] and load[Ordering.ACQUIRE], at compile time. Synchronized owns guarded data, and SyncView borrows it. try_read and try_write make one attempt and never wait. Check is_acquired before you consume the attempt with take. Several readers may hold the value at once; a writer excludes everyone else. The guard releases at scope exit or through release. A false is_acquired means Busy: the single attempt met a conflicting guard, a state that changed during the attempt, or the maximum reader count. Larecs does not retry. Record the unfinished work for a later pass, or skip the update only if your application can lose it.
data.write-a-separate-output-for-each-particl:
The stage uses the portable particle model and adds a Displacement component that belongs to each particle.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Displacement(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """A private output for one particle, avoiding a shared kernel counter.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]().write[ Displacement ]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Writes every per-row output before a later single-caller reduction. Args: context: Particle inputs and set-only displacement output. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() var dx = velocity.dx * time.delta var dy = velocity.dy * time.delta position.x += dx position.y += dy particle.set(Displacement(dx, dy)) write[Displacement]() grants set-only access, so the kernel must set the output on every row it visits. No two rows share an output, so the kernel needs no synchronization on any target. A resource or a mutable capture slot, by contrast, is one value that every invocation would write.

Split one particle movement call into chunks that run concurrently on host worker threads. Use this when a single kernel call covers many independent rows and profiling shows that the call dominates a step. Only the rows of one call are split; systems still run one after another in registration order. Threaded execution is experimental.
Start with Update entities with systems and kernels.
data.complete-program#Complete program: Complete program: examples/particles/threaded.mojo """Checks threaded particle movement against sequential host results.""" from std.testing import assert_almost_equal, assert_equal from larecs import ( Filter, KernelContext, Resources, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, World, ) from larecs import ThreadedExecutionConfig @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move[threaded: Bool](System): """Opts into host chunks for this movement kernel.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Moves disjoint rows and joins before returning. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If threaded eligibility or preparation fails. """ context.run[move, threaded=Self.threaded]() def run_stage[threaded: Bool](workers: Int) raises -> Position: """Checks parallel dispatch and whole-range fallback against exact values. Parameters: threaded: Whether to opt into the threaded engine. Args: workers: Submitted task budget; one exercises sequential fallback. Raises: Error: If configuration, execution, or a result check fails. Returns: Coordinate sums after two steps. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]( execution_config=ThreadedExecutionConfig( workers=workers, chunks_per_worker=2, min_parallel_rows=0 ) ) world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=4097) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move[threaded]()) scheduler.run(steps=2) var total = Position(0, 0) for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter](): ref position = particle.get[Position]() assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5) assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0) total.x += position.x total.y += position.y return total def main() raises: """Compares the sequential, one-worker, and multi-task call paths. Raises: Error: If an execution path disagrees. """ var sequential = run_stage[False](1) var fallback = run_stage[True](1) var threaded = run_stage[True](4) assert_equal(fallback.x, sequential.x) assert_equal(fallback.y, sequential.y) assert_equal(threaded.x, sequential.x) assert_equal(threaded.y, sequential.y) print( "PASS: sequential, one-worker fallback, and four-task particle parity" ) View the source on GitHub
data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Failure Cause and fix Threaded components require pointer-free trivial plain values An accessed component holds a pointer or owns memory, such as a List. Remove it from the filter, or keep that data in a portable resource. Threaded resources require pointer-free plain values or DevicePassableResource adapters A read resource owns memory or holds a pointer. Use a portable resource. Threaded resources require explicit read access The kernel declares an ordinary resource as writable, including through the Resources[Time]() read-write default. Declare it with read, or write per-row output as in Coordinate shared writes. Compile error for a lexical closure, captures, or DEVICE Threaded execution requires a thin kernel without capture slots on ExecutionBackend.HOST. ThreadedExecutionConfig raises workers and chunks_per_worker must be positive, their product must fit in an Int, and min_parallel_rows must not be negative. Structural lock exhaustion Each threaded call adds one structural lock to those already held, even when it runs sequentially. Live queries and selections, even empty ones, hold the others; end those you no longer need. No speedup Dispatch costs time; measure complete steps before you change the cutoff. Chunks are independent only in the rows they visit. Structural locks are not mutexes: shared state still needs a race-free write strategy. The threaded execution reference lists the remaining lock, alias, and failure rules.
data.how-larecs-splits-the-rows#How Larecs sp:
Larecs splits each matching physical store into kernel chunks: contiguous row ranges, each passed to one kernel invocation. Workers claim chunks in an unspecified order, and run returns only after every chunk has finished. This changes what code outside the row loop sees:
Code before or after the for loop runs once per chunk, not once per store. A row’s idx restarts at zero in each chunk; row indices are not entity IDs. Work that reads rows of other chunks needs a later run, after this call returns. Work mapping explains how Larecs sizes chunks.
data.move-particles-in-threaded-chunks#Move p:
The stage uses the portable particle model and the movement kernel from the first simulation.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta move is a thin kernel: a named def function that run receives as a compile-time parameter, as in context.run[move](). It captures no local variables and declares no capture slots; threaded execution requires both. Each row writes only its own Position, so no two chunks write the same data. Resources().read[Time]() declares Time read-only, so all chunks share one immutable value.
Opt in for one call with threaded=True:
@fieldwise_init struct Move[threaded: Bool](System): """Opts into host chunks for this movement kernel.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Moves disjoint rows and joins before returning. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If threaded eligibility or preparation fails. """ context.run[move, threaded=Self.threaded]() Then give the world more than one worker:
def run_stage[threaded: Bool](workers: Int) raises -> Position: """Checks parallel dispatch and whole-range fallback against exact values. Parameters: threaded: Whether to opt into the threaded engine. Args: workers: Submitted task budget; one exercises sequential fallback. Raises: Error: If configuration, execution, or a result check fails. Returns: Coordinate sums after two steps. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity]( execution_config=ThreadedExecutionConfig( workers=workers, chunks_per_worker=2, min_parallel_rows=0 ) ) world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = world.storage.add_entities(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=4097) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move[threaded]()) scheduler.run(steps=2) var total = Position(0, 0) for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter](): ref position = particle.get[Position]() assert_almost_equal(position.x, 0.5) assert_almost_equal(position.y, 1.0) total.x += position.x total.y += position.y return total def main() raises: """Compares the sequential, one-worker, and multi-task call paths. Raises: Error: If an execution path disagrees. """ var sequential = run_stage[False](1) var fallback = run_stage[True](1) var threaded = run_stage[True](4) assert_equal(fallback.x, sequential.x) assert_equal(fallback.y, sequential.y) assert_equal(threaded.x, sequential.x) assert_equal(threaded.y, sequential.y) print( "PASS: sequential, one-worker fallback, and four-task particle parity" ) ThreadedExecutionConfig sets the number of tasks Larecs submits per call, not reserved cores. chunks_per_worker=2 targets two chunks per worker, and min_parallel_rows=0 removes the row cutoff, so the 4097 particles split into chunks. The driver runs the same two steps three times, each in a fresh world: sequentially, threaded with one worker, and threaded with four workers.
From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/threaded.mojo The program prints a PASS line when all three runs move every particle to (0.5, 1.0).
data.next-steps#Next steps: Execute on a device runs the same kernel on an accelerator. Coordinate shared writes combines results from many chunks. Measure complete simulation steps before you keep threading.
data.variations#Variations:
Keep small calls sequential The default configuration has one worker, four chunks per worker, and a cutoff of 65,536 matched rows. With one worker, or with fewer matched rows than min_parallel_rows, a threaded=True call runs sequentially, once per physical store or selected range. Keep threaded=True in the system and set the worker budget per world; the compile-time eligibility checks apply either way.
Run threaded on a selection EntitySelection.run accepts the same threaded=True parameter and splits only the selection’s rows.
Read an owning collection Ordinary resources in a threaded call must be read-only values without pointers or owned memory. To read a list or buffer, wrap it in a portable resource.

Measure and tune a simulation starts with checked particle results, then measures complete steps and profiles dominant systems. Use it after the core simulation, before choosing threading, device execution, copy reuse, or spatial maintenance cadence.
Implementation benchmark methodology, regression operation, and scoped reports live under Inside Larecs. Reports retain their recorded workload, compiler, revision, hardware, and limitations.

Check equal simulation work first, then measure complete steps and profile the system that dominates them. Start with the first simulation. Optional targets must pass parity before timings influence your choice. A smaller kernel time alone does not establish a faster simulation.
data.capture-a-tracy-trace#Capture a Tracy tr:
Build a separate tracing binary inside Pixi’s environment so the linker sees the installed bindings and native library:
pixi run sh -c 'mojo build -I src -Xlinker -L"$CONDA_PREFIX/lib" -Xlinker -lmojotracy -DTRACY_ENABLED examples/particles/measurement.mojo -o /tmp/larecs-particles-tracy' pixi run tracy-profiler In Tracy, start discovery with Connect, then run /tmp/larecs-particles-tracy in another terminal. Inspect particles.complete_steps, particles.Move, and the internal zones for dominant work and repeated preparation. The twenty measured steps may be short; use a longer representative application run for profiling. Keep traced timings separate from optimized untraced comparison samples. pixi run profiling traces the repository’s benchmark suite instead of this particle driver.
data.establish-a-checked-workload#Establish a:
The measurement stage uses plain particle values and fixed time.
@fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 Keeping the same fields, precision, entity count, and step length makes target comparisons meaningful. Validate every output needed by the application; a sum alone can hide compensating per-entity errors.
Use the unchanged movement loop as the measured work.
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta Each step reads velocity and time and updates both position coordinates. Do not compare it with a variant that omits one coordinate, maintenance, or an output that the real application needs.
data.keep-results-with-their-conditions#Keep:
Link measurements with their workload, hardware, compiler, revision, method, uncertainty, and excluded costs. The host-dispatch investigation, partition comparison, and resource execution report provide scoped evidence. They do not predict the best target or layout on another machine.
Problem Next check Results differ Compare independent initial worlds, access declarations, write-only initialization and shared writes before timing. Disable copy reuse while diagnosing stale data. Device reports SKIP Record host coverage separately; a hardware skip is not device execution. Trace has no events Rebuild the final application with -DTRACY_ENABLED and the library flags, and connect the profiler before the run. Tiny or inconsistent timings Increase representative work, warm up, use repeated paired samples, and separate setup/output from the interval. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Provides a named application zone around the movement invocation.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Runs one synchronous kernel inside a Tracy zone. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If resource preparation or execution fails. """ with Zone("particles.Move"): context.run[move]() def main() raises: """Warms the simulation, times complete updates, and checks equal work. Raises: Error: If setup, stepping, or the final correctness check fails. """ var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity]() scheduler.world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = scheduler.world.storage.add_entities( Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=4097 ) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.initialize() scheduler.update(steps=5) # warmup is outside the measured interval var start = perf_counter_ns() with Zone("particles.complete_steps"): scheduler.update(steps=20) var elapsed = perf_counter_ns() - start scheduler.finalize() # Validation and output are outside the timer. var count = 0 for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter](): assert_almost_equal(particle.get[Position]().x, 6.25) assert_almost_equal(particle.get[Position]().y, 12.5) count += 1 assert_equal(count, 4097) print("PASS: 4097 particles after 25 steps") print("Measured 20 complete host steps (ns):", elapsed) View the source on GitHub
data.measure-complete-updates-separately-from:
The driver warms five steps, times twenty complete scheduler updates, and validates all 4097 particle results outside the interval.
def main() raises: """Warms the simulation, times complete updates, and checks equal work. Raises: Error: If setup, stepping, or the final correctness check fails. """ var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity]() scheduler.world.resources.add(Time(0.25)) _ = scheduler.world.storage.add_entities( Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 2), count=4097 ) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.initialize() scheduler.update(steps=5) # warmup is outside the measured interval var start = perf_counter_ns() with Zone("particles.complete_steps"): scheduler.update(steps=20) var elapsed = perf_counter_ns() - start scheduler.finalize() # Validation and output are outside the timer. var count = 0 for particle in scheduler.world.storage.query[move_filter](): assert_almost_equal(particle.get[Position]().x, 6.25) assert_almost_equal(particle.get[Position]().y, 12.5) count += 1 assert_equal(count, 4097) print("PASS: 4097 particles after 25 steps") print("Measured 20 complete host steps (ns):", elapsed) The interval includes system dispatch and synchronous run costs. It excludes compilation, world creation, initialization, warmup, finalization, validation, and printing. Each particle must finish at (6.25, 12.5) after all 25 steps. This small driver teaches timing boundaries; its single elapsed sample is not a performance claim or a backend benchmark.
From the repository root, build once and run the binary for repeated samples:
pixi run mojo build -I src examples/particles/measurement.mojo -o /tmp/larecs-particles /tmp/larecs-particles The program prints a correctness PASS and a machine-local elapsed nanosecond count. Record compilation separately. For a comparison, keep compiler version, optimization flags, hardware, workload, and revision fixed, warm each variant, alternate their order, and collect repeated paired samples without competing jobs. Use optimized builds without tracing, debug info, or sanitizers for timing. Follow the benchmark methodology for uncertainty, retained evidence, and regression checks.
data.profile-the-dominant-system#Profile the:
The system adds an application-level Tracy zone around its complete run call.
@fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Provides a named application zone around the movement invocation.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Runs one synchronous kernel inside a Tracy zone. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If resource preparation or execution fails. """ with Zone("particles.Move"): context.run[move]() particles.Move includes binding and execution, not only row arithmetic. Larecs also instruments internal work through Tracy. Compare system totals and call counts before changing a loop; time saved in a minor system has limited effect on a complete step. A host submission zone does not measure device kernel time in isolation; use a backend profiler for device activity and transfer details.
data.respect-explicit-simd-limits#Respect exp: Columns store one component struct per row: Position.x/y are fields in a Position column, not separate scalar columns. The public systems API exposes row iteration and no explicit CPU SIMD-batch interface. SIMD fields and compiler optimization do not create such an interface. Keep kernels on KernelContext rather than reaching into archetype storage to force a batch layout. Profile generated work before attributing a result to vectorization.
data.separate-arithmetic-from-boundary-costs#: Measurement boundary Include when comparing complete steps Sequential host Scheduler/system work, resource binding, store traversal, row processing, and required output handling. Threaded host The same work plus job preparation/dispatch/join; measure fallback and useful row-count thresholds. Device Packing, allocations when needed, input uploads, kernel launch/work, synchronization, downloads, and host scatter/publication. Copy reuse Validation and revisions, uploads that remain stale, mandatory output download, and invalidation caused by host edits or changing pack offsets. Spatial locality Input writes/dirty tracking, classification, sorting or partition transfer, location repair, and the passes that use the layout. Measure isolated kernels or maintenance passes to locate costs, then confirm the full-step result. A device can save arithmetic time while losing to transfers; a partitioned layout can improve one pass while increasing scan/binding costs. Keep maintenance inside the timed step when the real application requires it. Do not amortize a refresh across more steps than the correctness policy permits. After every change, rerun output checks and compare complete-step samples.
