Store a value that exists once per world, such as the step length, as a resource, and let kernels and systems read or change it. Share time and configuration runs this code.
@fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """The simulated time that passes in one step.""" var delta: Float64 """Step length.""" @fieldwise_init struct Configuration(Copyable, Movable): """Shared configuration for subsequent movement steps.""" var delta: Float64 """Configured step length.""" @fieldwise_init struct ConfigureTime(System): """Sets the step length before movement.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Reads configuration and updates shared time. Args: context: Access to the simulation resources. Raises: Error: If a required resource is missing. """ ref resources = context.world[].resources resources.get[Time]().delta = resources.get[Configuration]().delta var world = World[Position, Velocity]() world.resources.add(Time(delta=0.1), Configuration(delta=0.25)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) _ = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-3, -3)) Time and Configuration are resources. world.resources.add stores one value of each, and ConfigureTime changes Time through context.world[].resources before every movement step.

ResourceStorage manages the world’s resources:
Method Effect Raises when ResourceStorage.add Inserts values A type is already present ResourceStorage.get Returns a reference to the value The type is missing ResourceStorage.set Replaces existing values Any type is missing; then no value changes. With add_if_not_found=True, it inserts missing types instead. ResourceStorage.remove Removes values A type is missing Do not keep a resource reference across removal or replacement.

Args: context: The matching rows and the declared resources. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta A kernel declares its resources with Resources, separately from its component filter:
Declaration Access through the kernel read[T]() Read with get read_write[T]() Read and write with get write[T]() Write with set only, on the host; device kernels reject it Resources[T]() Read and write, like read_write Every declared resource must exist in the world when you call SystemContext.run; otherwise run raises.
On the sequential host, a resource can own collections such as a List. Every kernel call in one run sees the same resource value. Because one run can call the kernel several times, change per-step values in a system’s update, as ConfigureTime does, rather than in the kernel.
data.define-a-resource#Define a resource: A resource is a struct that conforms to resource.ResourceType, which requires Copyable and Deinitable. Copyable, Movable satisfies both. A world holds at most one value per resource type, and resource types do not appear in the world’s component list.
data.next-steps#Next steps:
Use portable resources covers threaded and device restrictions and adapters for resources that own data.
Bindings, transfers, and revisions explains source leases, invocation-owned views, and publication.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Fix run raises because Time is missing Add Time with world.resources.add before you start the scheduler. Compile error on resource access Check the kernel’s Resources declaration; the component filter does not grant resource access.

data.add-and-remove-components#Add and remove: world.storage.add(marker, Velocity(0, 1)) assert_true(world.storage.has[Velocity](marker)) world.storage.remove[Velocity](marker) assert_false(world.storage.has[Velocity](marker)) HostStorage.add and HostStorage.remove accept any number of components. Each call is a structural change: the entity moves to the storage for its new composition.
data.check-whether-an-entity-has-a-component#: assert_true(world.storage.has[Velocity](walker)) assert_false(world.storage.has[Velocity](marker)) with assert_raises(): _ = world.storage.get[Velocity](marker) get raises when the entity lacks the component. Check with HostStorage.has first when the composition is not known.
data.failure-behavior#Failure behavior: with assert_raises(): world.storage.set(marker, Velocity(1, 1)) with assert_raises(): world.storage.remove[Velocity](marker) var positions = world.storage.query[Filter().include[Position]()]() with assert_raises(): world.storage.add(marker, Velocity(1, 1)) assert_equal(len(positions), 2) world.storage.remove_entity(marker) with assert_raises(): _ = world.storage.get[Position](marker) with assert_raises(): world.storage.add(walker, Frozen(0)) Situation Result The entity was removed Every operation on its handle raises. get, set, or remove names a component the entity lacks The call raises. add names a component the entity already has The call raises. A query or selection holds a structural lock add, remove, and replace raise; release the query or close the with block first.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Create and remove entities in batches changes many entities with one call. Update entities with systems and kernels runs the same change on every matching entity.
data.read-and-change-a-component#Read and cha: ref position = world.storage.get[Position](walker) position.x = 5 assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Position](walker).x, 5) world.storage.get[Position](walker) = Position(10, 0) assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Position](walker).x, 10) HostStorage.get returns a mutable reference to the component. You can change a field through it or assign a whole new value. The reference borrows the world, so get it again after you add or remove components.
data.replace-components-in-one-move#Replace c: world.storage.replace[Velocity]().by(Frozen(2), entity=walker) assert_false(world.storage.has[Velocity](walker)) assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Frozen](walker).speed, 2) HostStorage.replace names the components to remove, and Replacer.by supplies the components to add. The entity moves to its new storage once. A separate remove followed by add moves it twice.
data.run-the-complete-program#Run the complet:
Complete program: examples/particles/single_entity.mojo """Reads, changes, adds, removes, and replaces components of single particles. Region markers supply excerpts for the single-entity guide. """ from std.testing import ( assert_almost_equal, assert_equal, assert_false, assert_raises, assert_true, ) from larecs import Filter, World @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable): """Where a particle is.""" var x: Float64 """Horizontal coordinate.""" var y: Float64 """Vertical coordinate.""" @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable): """How far a particle moves per unit of time.""" var dx: Float64 """Horizontal speed.""" var dy: Float64 """Vertical speed.""" @fieldwise_init struct Frozen(Copyable, Movable): """Marks a particle that stopped and remembers its last speed.""" var speed: Float64 """Speed before the particle froze.""" def main() raises: """Changes single particles and checks every result. Raises: Error: If an operation or a result check fails. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity, Frozen]() var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var marker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(3, 3)) ref position = world.storage.get[Position](walker) position.x = 5 assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Position](walker).x, 5) world.storage.get[Position](walker) = Position(10, 0) assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Position](walker).x, 10) assert_true(world.storage.has[Velocity](walker)) assert_false(world.storage.has[Velocity](marker)) with assert_raises(): _ = world.storage.get[Velocity](marker) world.storage.set(walker, Position(0, 0), Velocity(2, 0)) assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Velocity](walker).dx, 2) world.storage.add(marker, Velocity(0, 1)) assert_true(world.storage.has[Velocity](marker)) world.storage.remove[Velocity](marker) assert_false(world.storage.has[Velocity](marker)) world.storage.replace[Velocity]().by(Frozen(2), entity=walker) assert_false(world.storage.has[Velocity](walker)) assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Frozen](walker).speed, 2) with assert_raises(): world.storage.set(marker, Velocity(1, 1)) with assert_raises(): world.storage.remove[Velocity](marker) var positions = world.storage.query[Filter().include[Position]()]() with assert_raises(): world.storage.add(marker, Velocity(1, 1)) assert_equal(len(positions), 2) world.storage.remove_entity(marker) with assert_raises(): _ = world.storage.get[Position](marker) with assert_raises(): world.storage.add(walker, Frozen(0)) assert_equal(len(world), 1) print("PASS: single-particle reads, changes, and composition changes") View the source on GitHub
Run it from the repository root:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/single_entity.mojo It prints PASS: single-particle reads, changes, and composition changes.
data.set-several-components-at-once#Set sever: world.storage.set(walker, Position(0, 0), Velocity(2, 0)) assert_almost_equal(world.storage.get[Velocity](walker).dx, 2) HostStorage.set assigns new values to components the entity already has. It does not add missing components.

This page keeps the links to an earlier guide working. Each section points to
the page that covers the topic now.

Maintain particle locality groups the particles of each grid cell in memory without changing entity identity, and selects exactly one cell’s particles. Start with kernel access and scoped selections.
For classifier and maintenance contracts, use the spatial reference. Spatial maintenance internals explains dirty tracking, classification, and partition placement.

Keep particles of the same grid cell next to each other in memory, and select exactly the particles of one cell. Use this when profiling shows that a pass reads nearby particles together and suffers from scattered rows. Grouping changes only where rows live; entity handles and component values stay the same. It does not find exact neighbors.
Start with Update entities with systems and kernels and Create and remove entities in batches.
data.choose-a-placement-policy#Choose a place:
Registering the classifier chooses how Larecs groups rows; it does not move rows by itself. The driver runs the same setup under both policies:
def run_stage[partitioned: Bool]() raises: """Checks the same identities and values under both placement policies. Parameters: partitioned: Choose growable cluster stores instead of row ordering. Raises: Error: If classification, selection, movement, or checks fail. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]() world.resources.add(Time(1)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.5, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(1.5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) var excluded = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-1, 0), Int32(1)) world.register_spatial_classifier[spatial_filter]( Grid(cell_size=1), partitioned=partitioned ) world.maintain_spatial() assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5) assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](excluded).x, -1) Policy Placement after maintenance partitioned=False (default) Larecs sorts the classified rows of each physical store by key, so equal keys become contiguous. The order of equal keys is unspecified. partitioned=True, called partition mode Each cluster of each logical archetype gets its own physical store, a partition, which starts with room for one row and doubles as it fills. Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.
The same logical archetype supports two placement policies.
Letters label entities, and colors and key labels mark clusters. All components and the entity ID of a row move together. In partition mode, a new particle, or one whose components changed, waits in a staging store: a physical store for rows that the next maintenance pass will place. Queries and kernels still visit staged rows.
data.complete-program#Complete program: Complete program: examples/particles/spatial.mojo """Checks explicit spatial maintenance and exact particle cluster selection.""" from std.testing import assert_almost_equal, assert_equal from larecs import ( ExecutionBackend, Filter, KernelContext, Resources, Scheduler, System, SystemContext, World, ) from std.testing import assert_raises from larecs import SpatialClassifier, grid_cell, morton_key_3d from larecs.entity import EntityAccessor @fieldwise_init struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic.""" var x: Float32 var y: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable): """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time.""" var dx: Float32 var dy: Float32 @fieldwise_init struct Time(Copyable, Movable): """Shared simulated step length.""" var delta: Float32 comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta comptime spatial_filter = Filter().read[Position]().exclude[Int32]() @fieldwise_init struct Grid(SpatialClassifier): """Classifies eligible particles by a bounded planar Morton cell.""" comptime Accessor = EntityAccessor[spatial_filter] var cell_size: Float64 def classify(self, entity: Self.Accessor) raises -> UInt64: """Reads only the declared position input. Args: entity: Borrowed classifier inputs; never retained. Raises: Error: If the cell width, coordinates, or cell bounds are invalid. Returns: The exact cell's Morton key. """ ref position = entity.get[Position]() return morton_key_3d( grid_cell(Float64(position.x), self.cell_size), grid_cell(Float64(position.y), self.cell_size), ) @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Moves particles and then refreshes their physical placement.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Runs explicit maintenance after movement completes. Args: context: Access to the unlocked world. Raises: Error: If execution or maintenance fails. """ context.run[move]() context.world[].maintain_spatial() def run_stage[partitioned: Bool]() raises: """Checks the same identities and values under both placement policies. Parameters: partitioned: Choose growable cluster stores instead of row ordering. Raises: Error: If classification, selection, movement, or checks fail. """ var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]() world.resources.add(Time(1)) var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.5, 0), Velocity(1, 0)) var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(1.5, 0), Velocity(0, 2)) var excluded = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-1, 0), Int32(1)) world.register_spatial_classifier[spatial_filter]( Grid(cell_size=1), partitioned=partitioned ) world.maintain_spatial() assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5) assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](excluded).x, -1) comptime if partitioned: # New rows are visible to ordinary execution while still staged. var staged = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.25, 0)) assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]()]()), 4) var context = SystemContext(world) with assert_raises(): _ = context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()]( morton_key_3d(0, 0) ) world.maintain_spatial() var clean_context = SystemContext(world) var selected = clean_context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()]( morton_key_3d(0, 0) ) assert_equal( len(selected), 2 ) # walker and staged; two logical archetypes selected.run[move]() # only walker has Velocity assert_equal(len(selected), 2) # membership stays fixed after the write selected^.release() world.maintain_spatial() assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 1.5) assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](staged).x, 0.25) var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Int32](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=1) assert_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](climber).y, 2) assert_equal( scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, Float32(2.5) if partitioned else Float32(1.5), ) def main() raises: """Checks grid bounds, default ordering, and partitioned selections. Raises: Error: If any spatial contract check fails. """ assert_equal(grid_cell(-0.1, 1), -1) with assert_raises(): _ = grid_cell(1048576, 1) with assert_raises(): _ = morton_key_3d(0, -1048577) run_stage[False]() run_stage[True]() print("PASS: row ordering, partition staging, exact selections, and bounds") View the source on GitHub
data.failures-and-limits#Failures and limits: Failure Cause and fix maintain_spatial or select_cluster raises a locked-world error A query, selection, or storage range is still alive, possibly an empty one. End it first. Cluster selection requires clean spatial maintenance Particles are dirty or staged. Release old selections, call maintain_spatial, then select again. Cluster selection requires partitioned spatial storage Register the classifier with partitioned=True. grid_cell or morton_key_3d raises A coordinate is not finite, the cell width is not positive, or a cell lies outside the supported range. Change the cell width or the key encoding. maintain_spatial raises a classifier error Larecs keeps the previous rows, keys, and dirty marks. Fix the input and call it again. Particles stay in old clusters after raw writes Larecs could not see the write. Mark the particles dirty or invalidate, then maintain. The spatial reference lists classifier rules, key bounds, and the exact maintenance contract. The partition benchmark records measurements for one workload, not a general speed guarantee.
data.maintain-placement-after-movement#Mainta:
Movement and maintenance stay separate steps:
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length. Args: context: Matching rows and read-only time. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Moves particles and then refreshes their physical placement.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Runs explicit maintenance after movement completes. Args: context: Access to the unlocked world. Raises: Error: If execution or maintenance fails. """ context.run[move]() context.world[].maintain_spatial() move declares Position writable, so Larecs marks every classified particle it visits as dirty: its key may be out of date. Positions change immediately, but rows move only when you call World.maintain_spatial. Then Larecs classifies each dirty particle once, using its final position, and moves rows to match the new keys. Kernels and systems never run maintenance by themselves.
Maintenance moves rows, so the world must be unlocked. End every query and selection first, because empty queries and selections hold locks. Discard component references before maintenance, and look components up again by entity handle afterwards.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Spatial maintenance internals explains dirty tracking, classification, and partition placement. Measure complete simulation steps to decide whether locality pays off.
data.select-one-cluster#Select one cluster:
Partition mode can select exactly the particles with one key:
comptime if partitioned: # New rows are visible to ordinary execution while still staged. var staged = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.25, 0)) assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]()]()), 4) var context = SystemContext(world) with assert_raises(): _ = context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()]( morton_key_3d(0, 0) ) world.maintain_spatial() var clean_context = SystemContext(world) var selected = clean_context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()]( morton_key_3d(0, 0) ) assert_equal( len(selected), 2 ) # walker and staged; two logical archetypes selected.run[move]() # only walker has Velocity assert_equal(len(selected), 2) # membership stays fixed after the write selected^.release() world.maintain_spatial() assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 1.5) assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](staged).x, 0.25) SystemContext.select_cluster needs partition mode, a clean maintenance state, and an unlocked world; that is why the first attempt, made while staged waits in the staging store, raises. The selection contains walker and staged, which share key (0, 0) but belong to different logical archetypes; only walker has a Velocity and matches move. The membership stays fixed until you release the selection, even after walker moves to another cell. The selection matches the key exactly, not a radius, and adjacent keys need not be adjacent cells. For exact neighbors, check the actual distances in the cells you need, or build a separate spatial index.
The driver checks the grid bounds and both policies:
def main() raises: """Checks grid bounds, default ordering, and partitioned selections. Raises: Error: If any spatial contract check fails. """ assert_equal(grid_cell(-0.1, 1), -1) with assert_raises(): _ = grid_cell(1048576, 1) with assert_raises(): _ = morton_key_3d(0, -1048577) run_stage[False]() run_stage[True]() print("PASS: row ordering, partition staging, exact selections, and bounds") From the repository root, run:
pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/spatial.mojo The PASS line means both policies placed and selected the particles as expected on the host.
data.variations#Variations:
Choose a maintenance cadence A pass with no dirty particles returns without touching rows. Otherwise it classifies only the dirty particles, but it still copies one key per entity slot, scans store metadata, and moves every row whose placement changes, with all of its components. Structural changes make the next pass reclassify every particle. Maintaining every few steps instead of every step trades placement accuracy for fewer row moves. Measure complete steps to choose, and compare the locality-sensitive pass on its own as well.
Report writes that Larecs cannot see Larecs marks particles dirty when you write positions through set, a mutable get, or a kernel that declares the write. Use read or read-only queries to look at positions without marking them. After a write through a raw pointer, call world.storage.mark_spatial_dirty(entity) for each changed particle, or World.invalidate_spatial to reclassify everything.
Move particles on a device Device movement marks the same particles dirty when it copies Position back. Maintenance and classification still run on the host afterwards.

data.create-entities-outside-a-system#Create: During setup, HostStorage.add_entities creates a batch directly in the world. It returns a locked row range for direct component access, not a selection, and has no run method. Inside systems, use context.add_entities to get a selection.
data.empty-and-invalid-batches#Empty and inva: add_entities with count=0 returns an empty selection that still holds a lock. Running a kernel on an empty selection never runs the kernel body. A negative count raises.
data.end-the-structural-lock-with-with#End th:
Create a batch of entities, change their components, and run kernels on only those entities with a scoped selection. Then remove entities once the scope ends. Create and remove particles runs this code and checks the result.
def reset_position(context: KernelContext[Filter().write[Position]()]): """Initializes every selected position without reading it. Args: context: Selected rows with write-only Position access. """ for particle in context: particle.set(Position(0, 0)) @fieldwise_init struct Spawn(System): """Creates and moves only the new particles at initialization.""" def initialize(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Creates a scoped batch. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. Raises: Error: If creation or movement fails. """ with context.add_entities(Position(9, 9), count=3) as selected: selected.add(Velocity(1, 0)) selected.run[reset_position]() selected.run[move]() context.world[].storage.remove_entities[ Filter().include[Position]().exclude[Velocity]() ]() def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Leaves creation to initialization. Args: context: Access to the simulation world. """ pass context.add_entities creates three particles and returns a selection of exactly those three. Inside the with block, selected.add, selected.run, and other selection methods act on those particles only. After the block, remove_entities deletes every particle with a Position and no Velocity.
Values versus structure Assigning position.x in a kernel changes a value. Creating or deleting an entity, or adding or removing a component type, changes the world’s structure. A structural change can move rows in memory. After one, discard component references and row accessors, and look components up again by entity handle.
Select exactly the entities you change These operations return an EntitySelection:
SystemContext.add_entities selects exactly the new entities. SystemContext.add, SystemContext.remove, and SystemContext.replace select the entities that match the filter you pass. A selection keeps its members when their components change. Its add, remove, and replace methods change the members’ components in place and return nothing; remove removes components, not entities. Its run method visits the members that also match the kernel’s filter, and never other entities with the same components.
EntitySelection documents every selection method.
End the structural lock with with A selection holds a structural lock until it is released. While any lock is held, unrelated entity creation, entity deletion, and component additions or removals raise a locked-world error.
Use with so the lock ends when the block ends, including on an error or an early return. To scope a selection you already hold, write with selection^ as selected:. Inside with, the lock lasts until the block ends, even if you release the bound selection earlier. Without with, the lock ends when you call the consuming release method or the selection is destroyed. Selections are movable but not copyable.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Update entities with systems and kernels compares selections with queries and entity handles. Change one entity’s components shows the single-entity storage operations. Structural transitions traces typed movement, swap-removal, and entity-location repair.
data.remove-entities#Remove entities: HostStorage.remove_entity deletes one entity by handle, and HostStorage.remove_entities deletes every entity that matches a filter. SystemContext has no method for deleting entities, so a system deletes through context.world[].storage, as Spawn does. Delete only after the with block ends; while the selection’s lock is held, deletion raises a locked-world error.

data:
Put repeated simulation work in a system, and let the system run a kernel over every entity that matches a filter. This page uses the movement code from Your first simulation.
comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]() comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]() def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]): """Advances every particle by its velocity times the step length. Args: context: The matching rows and the declared resources. """ ref time = context.resources.get[Time]() for particle in context: ref position = particle.get[Position]() ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]() position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta @fieldwise_init struct Move(System): """Runs the `move` kernel once per step.""" def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises: """Moves all particles. Args: context: Access to the scheduler's world. Raises: Error: If `Time` is missing from the world. """ context.run[move]() var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity](world^) scheduler.add_system(Move()) scheduler.run(steps=10) move is the kernel, Move is the system that runs it, and the Scheduler calls Move.update once per step.
data.compare-handles-queries-and-selections#C: Value Copy and move Structural lock Use Entity handle Copyable and movable None Identify an entity in storage calls; survives row movement, not deletion Query row accessor Movable, not copyable Held by its query Read the query’s components; discard before structural changes Query Copy: own cursor and lock. Move: transfers the lock Until destroyed, even when exhausted or empty Read-only traversal Entity selection Movable, not copyable Until released, destroyed, or its with block ends, even when empty Change components and run kernels on exactly its members Storage batch range (HostStorage.add_entities) Copy: own cursor and lock. Move: transfers the lock Until destroyed, even when exhausted or empty Low-level traversal and mutable unsafe_get; no run Create and remove entities in batches covers selections.
data.declare-component-and-resource-access#De:
A Filter selects entities and sets how the kernel may access their components:
Step Matches Access through the kernel include[T]() Entities with T Read and write with get read[T]() Entities with T Read with get write[T]() Entities with T Write with set only exclude[T]() Entities without T None exclusive() Only entities without further components Unchanged The kernel’s KernelContext exposes only the declared access. Calling get on a component the filter does not guarantee, or writing through read access, fails to compile. Resources declares resource access separately; see Share values with resources.
data.how-often-a-kernel-runs#How often a kern: On the host, SystemContext.run calls the kernel once for each non-empty matching physical store: a group of rows with the same components. One logical archetype can have several physical stores. Put per-entity work inside the for loop over the context. With no matching entities, the kernel body never runs. All calls finish before run returns, so the next system sees the results.
data.inspect-entities-outside-a-kernel#Inspec:
Use HostStorage.query to read entities outside a kernel, for example during setup. Create and remove particles inspects the marker before it starts the scheduler:
var query = world.storage.query[ Filter().read[Position]().exclude[Velocity]() ]() var query_copy = query.copy() for row in query^: assert_almost_equal(row.get[Position]().x, -3.0) assert_equal(row.get_entity(), marker) for _ in query_copy^: pass assert_equal( len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]().exclusive()]()), 1 ) Each query row is an ArchetypeRowAccessor, not an entity handle. get reads a component the filter guarantees, and get_entity returns the entity’s handle. A query is read-only, even when its filter uses include; use a kernel to change values. exclusive() restricts a query to entities with exactly the listed components, so the last assertion counts only marker.
A live query holds a structural lock until it ends; empty and exhausted queries still hold it. Consume it in a short loop, or let it go out of scope, before you create or remove entities. A copy starts at the same position with its own cursor and lock; a move transfers the existing lock. The example copies the query to show this, and consumes both with ^ so their locks end before the scheduler takes the world. Do not keep a row accessor beyond its query or across structural changes. Structural locks protect references from invalidation; they are not mutexes.
data.next-steps#Next steps: Execution covers captures, portable resources, threaded host kernels, and device execution. HostStorage and ArchetypeRowAccessor document lower-level traversal. Execution and ownership explains scheduler and context lifetimes; queries and ranges explains cursor metadata and structural guards.
data.order-systems-and-steps#Order systems an:
System has three hooks: initialize, update, and finalize. Scheduler.run initializes all systems, updates them once per step, and then finalizes them. Within each phase, systems run in the order you added them.
An error in a hook propagates out of run, and the remaining hooks do not run: if initialize or update raises, finalize is skipped. To step the simulation in several batches, call initialize, update(steps=...), and finalize yourself.
data.troubleshooting#Troubleshooting: Symptom Cause and fix run raises about a missing resource The kernel declares a resource the world lacks. Add it during setup. Compile error on component access The filter does not guarantee the component, or grants only read access. Adjust the filter. Locked-world error A query or selection is still alive. End its scope before the structural change.
data.write-values-without-reading-them#Write:
def reset_position(context: KernelContext[Filter().write[Position]()]): """Initializes every selected position without reading it. Args: context: Selected rows with write-only Position access. """ for particle in context: particle.set(Position(0, 0)) Filter.write permits EntityAccessor.set and rejects get. Set the component on every row the kernel visits; a later kernel can then read it. Create and remove particles runs this kernel before movement.
For device execution, the access mode decides the transfers: read access uploads values, write access downloads results, and read-write access does both. Write-only values are not uploaded. See device execution for target limits.

data: Architecture explains how storage, ownership, and execution fit together. Development covers changing and checking those mechanisms. Application tasks start in the guides; exact public contracts live in the reference.

We separate world-owned state from the temporary views used to execute work. These explanations trace the implementation behind the application contracts.
Mechanism Explanation Execution and ownership Scheduler phases, world ownership, system borrows, and kernel views. Archetypes, columns, and locations Logical composition, physical stores, typed lifecycles, and structural movement. Queries, selections, and ranges Shared metadata, independent cursors, exact membership, and structural guards. Work mapping Sequential ranges, threaded chunks, and packed grid-stride execution. Bindings, transfers, and revisions Source leases, adapter views, publication, and device-copy validity. Spatial maintenance Dirty identities, classification boundaries, permutations, and partition placement. Synchronization internals Atomic scope, guard state, confinement, and unsupported bindings. The design and evidence map links the existing requirements, decisions, and research with their status intact. An accepted decision can contain unimplemented parts; the explanations above describe verified source behavior. Experimental API status stays in compatibility and status.

run selects a compile-time ExecutionBackend, defaulting to HOST. A thin kernel can use either target. Value-taking callables use the sequential host; threaded host execution requires an eligible nonraising thin kernel. DEVICE validates support and a working context even when no rows match, and has no host fallback.
The mapping diagram follows two physical ranges through all three executors.
Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.
Ranges remain separate on the host; device work uses a packed row domain.
Sequential host execution binds resources once and traverses nonempty matching physical stores. Each context contains pointers to its first row and a local length. Selected runs use the saved exact ranges. The iterator begins at zero and increments by one. Empty matches call no kernel, while resource validation and mutable adapter lifecycle work can still occur.
data.packed-device-iteration#Packed device it:
Device execution allocates or grows one buffer per accessed component type, packs matching spans, prepares resources/captures, and launches the kernel. EntityAccessorIterator starts each GPU thread at global_idx.x and advances by context.thread_count. A thread stops when its offset reaches the packed length. That grid-stride rule covers every row once, including when the launch has fewer threads than rows.
The current launch uses 256 threads per block. gpu_grid_dim starts with ceil(length / 256) and caps blocks with a thread-based device residency bound when device attributes are available. Missing attributes disable the cap. This bound ignores register and shared-memory usage; it is not an occupancy guarantee. The iterator performs no transfer or synchronization itself. Written spans return through staged transfers before run returns.
The diagram adapts the thesis’s host, threaded-host, and grid-stride figures; four device threads illustrate the indexing rule rather than the actual block size. Public restrictions and call forms are in the execution reference.
Implementation: Source, Source, Source, Source. Evidence: test/grid_stride_iterator_test.mojo, test/threaded_execution_test.mojo, test/gpu_launch_cap_test.mojo, test/check_execution_backend_contracts.py.
data.preparing-and-draining-threaded-jobs#Pre:
_run_threaded validates eligibility independently of fallback, retains active execution and structural guards, binds resources, and checks all ranges and integer limits. Selected ranges are checked for overlap on a sorted copy; the saved order remains available for fallback.
For enough rows and more than one configured worker, the target job count is workers * chunks_per_worker; chunk size is the ceiling of total matched rows divided by that target. Each range splits independently, so the actual job count can exceed the target. Every chunk gets offset column pointers and local indices. All fallible preparation finishes before kernels write rows.
Workers use an atomic UInt32 cursor to claim prepared contexts dynamically. There is no fixed store-to-thread assignment. parallelize schedules at most the configured worker count and joins before finalization and release. Below the row cutoff, or with one worker, calls retain whole-range sequential granularity; eligibility checks still apply. Row ownership prevents overlap between chunks, but shared mutable adapted data still requires its adapter’s concurrent-mutation contract.
